sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 6172.1 ± 143.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Whole-cell ELISA on non-permeabilized cells confirmed surface expression at levels comparable across all constructs; tagged receptors used for pharmacological assays (PMC13005129). CLIP-Lumi4Tb binding to intact cells confirmed surface delivery of HA-CLIP-hM3 RASSL (PMC4505543). Function preserved in pharmacological and FRET/BRET signaling studies.
sites.rationale: CHRM3 (UniProt P20309) has no signal peptide; residue 1 (M) is the first extracellular residue and the N-terminal domain spans residues 1–67, placing a prepended tag 67 residues from TM1 (starts at 68) — well clear of the >=3-residue TM boundary constraint. Three independent publications (PMC13005129, PMC4505543, PMC10960872) each report a tag (HA, HA+CLIP, FLAG respectively) at the N-terminus of the full-length membrane-anchored receptor expressed in mammalian or insect cells, with surface display confirmed on intact/non-permeabilized cells in two of the three studies. insert_after_residue=0 (prepend); residue_after=M (residue 1) read directly from the numbered sequence. PMC13005129: full-length human M3 muscarinic receptor bearing an N-terminal HA epitope tag expressed in mammalian cells; surface display confirmed by whole-cell ELISA on non-permeabilized cells detecting the extracellular HA tag, and by anti-HA-biotin antibody on intact cells. Constructs used for pharmacological studies. Independently corroborated by PMC4505543 (HA+CLIP tag at N-terminus of full-length hM3 RASSL, surface delivery confirmed by CLIP-Lumi4Tb binding to intact cells) and PMC10960872 (N-terminal FLAG tag on full-length human M3 receptor).

sources.claim: To confirm that all receptor constructs were expressed at similar levels on the cell surface, we employed a whole-cell ELISA strategy that can selectively detect the extracellular HA-tag fused to the N-terminus of all receptor constructs 32 , 38 .

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines were evaluated. L2, L3, L4 (PMC13005129), L5, L6, L7 (PMC4505543), and L8 (PMC10960872) all support the same N-terminal prepend position (insert_after_residue=0); L3 was chosen as the primary supporting clip because it most explicitly confirms extracellular surface display via whole-cell ELISA on non-permeabilized cells. L1 (ICL3 T4L replacement, residues 260–481) is an intracellular insertion used for crystallography and is recorded in other_positions. L8 also mentions a C-terminal His-tag, which maps to the intracellular C-terminus (residues 548–590) and is likewise recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an insertion in any extracellular loop (ECL1 126–142, ECL2 208–229, ECL3 514–527) of the full-length membrane-anchored receptor.

literature_other_positions.note: ICL3 residues 260–481 replaced with T4 lysozyme (residues 1–161) for crystallization; the entire replaced segment is within the intracellular loop (topology: intracellular 253–492).
C-terminal His-tag used for purification; the C-terminus (residues 548–590) is intracellular per topology landmarks.
